f.claim: The rename-staleness guarantee assumes that the name revision cannot be captured after candidate reads from an older name state, but the design does not establish that read-order or snapshot invariant.
f.location: Rename consistency; Candidate traversal and result shape; Validation
f.evidence: Spec reads name/all for filtered cursors, preserving existing high-water snapshot; no explicit candidate/revision read snapshot/order. Possible failure: skip nonmatching candidate, rename makes it match, then capture new revision, allowing continuation to skip match without staleness. Existing store serialization/read transaction could discharge assumption. SQLite isolation https://www.sqlite.org/isolation.html states reader continues to see unchanging snapshot within read transaction.

votes.evidence: Reproduce failure breaks at capturing new name revision after old candidate state: src/store/queries.rs::query_with_output_for_caller begins BEGIN DEFERRED before Command::Directory; connection stays in transaction throughout. src/store/connection.rs::open_query is separate read-only connection. SQLite https://www.sqlite.org/isolation.html explains that commits made during an active read transaction are invisible to it. Candidate names and name/all revision thus share snapshot. Continuation holds old revision then stales.

Refute (a) equivalent mechanism exists: src/store/queries.rs::query_with_output_for_caller BEGIN DEFERRED line 214 before directory dispatch line 277, spanning revision reads, candidates and cursor. SQLite https://www.sqlite.org/isolation.html confirms read transaction unchanging snapshot. (b) claimed skip would violate contract; (c) in scope; (d) material if possible, but read snapshot defeats premise. Design preserves existing query loop, so repeating boundary is documentation suggestion.

Ground premise fails: design preserves existing loop and snapshot; query_with_output_for_caller BEGIN DEFERRED before Command::Directory, transaction open throughout traversal/cursor. New name revision and candidate projections share read snapshot. SQLite primary https://www.sqlite.org/isolation.html explains that the snapshot remains stable for that read transaction. Concurrent rename cannot combine old names/new revision. Additional requirement merely restates invariant.
